description.content: Per-deployment data plane API. One vhost per Deployment under *.saas.omarss.net.

item.name: tenants

item.name: api-keys
item.description:
Tenant-bound bearer-token API keys (AGENTS.md §8.5). Plaintext
secrets are returned exactly once at create and rotate time;
subsequent reads expose only the visible prefix. argon2id PHC
hashing + envelope-encrypted prefix-search index per ADR 008.
Rotation preserves the previous secret for a configurable grace
window (default 24h, max 7d) so clients can roll over without
downtime.

item.name: Soft-revoke an API key (alias of revoke).
Fetch an API key by id (no plaintext).

header.description: Weak ETag from a prior GET; rejects on mismatch with 412.

item.name: Immediately revoke an API key (no grace).
/v1/api-keys/:api_key_id/rotate
item.description: Mints a new plaintext secret for the same row id and demotes the previous secret into a predecessor PHC valid until `predecessor_expires_at`. Requires `apikey.write` when SAAS_RBAC_ENFORCE_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

item.name: Rotate an API key with optional grace period.

request.description: Mints a new plaintext secret for the same row id and demotes the previous secret into a predecessor PHC valid until `predecessor_expires_at`. Requires `apikey.write` when SAAS_RBAC_ENFORCE_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

item.name: /v1/tenants/:tenant_id/api-keys
item.description: Creates an API key under the named tenant. The response body carries the plaintext bearer in `secret` — this is the only time it is returned. Subsequent reads expose only the prefix. The `apikey.write` permission is required when the deployment has SAAS_RBAC_ENFORCE_DESTRUCTIVE=true (Phase 8 retrofit).

item.name: Mint a new API key. Plaintext returned ONCE.

request.description: Creates an API key under the named tenant. The response body carries the plaintext bearer in `secret` — this is the only time it is returned. Subsequent reads expose only the prefix. The `apikey.write` permission is required when the deployment has SAAS_RBAC_ENFORCE_DESTRUCTIVE=true (Phase 8 retrofit).

item.name: social-providers
item.description:
Social login linking via Keycloak's IdP brokering. POST returns a
Keycloak-brokered authorization URL — the caller redirects there
and Keycloak completes the OAuth dance + writes the federated_identity
row itself. ADR 014 records the design.

item.name: /v1/users/:user_id/social-providers
item.description: Per ADR 014: we never call CreateUserFederatedIdentity from a user-facing endpoint (no proof-of-possession). Instead, the platform mints Keycloak's hashed link URL — the caller redirects the user's browser there and Keycloak completes the OAuth dance with the external IdP, writing the federated_identity row itself.

item.name: Start a social-provider link flow. Returns the Keycloak link URL.

request.description: Per ADR 014: we never call CreateUserFederatedIdentity from a user-facing endpoint (no proof-of-possession). Instead, the platform mints Keycloak's hashed link URL — the caller redirects the user's browser there and Keycloak completes the OAuth dance with the external IdP, writing the federated_identity row itself.

item.name: List linked social providers for a user.
Unlink a social provider. Emits user.social_unlinked.
authorization
item.description:
RBAC roles, permissions, member-role assignments, and the
synchronous check API. Uses Casbin's RBAC-with-domains model with
dom = tenant_id (ADR 005). Wildcard domains are forbidden by DB
CHECK + service-layer validation. Every denied check emits an
`authorization.denied` outbox event for the Phase 10 audit log.

item.name: Evaluate many checks in one call (max 100).
/v1/authorization/check
item.description: Synchronous policy check. Returns `allowed=true` plus the role that matched, or `allowed=false`. Denied checks emit an `authorization.denied` outbox event so the audit log records the attempt.

item.name: Evaluate a single (member, permission, tenant) check.

request.description: Synchronous policy check. Returns `allowed=true` plus the role that matched, or `allowed=false`. Denied checks emit an `authorization.denied` outbox event so the audit log records the attempt.

item.description:
Pending invitations for an Organization. POST returns 202 with the

item.name: /v1/invitations/:invitation_id/accept
item.description: Consumes a one-time accept token. The caller's JWT supplies the user identity; the invitation's stored tenant_id is constant-time-compared to the caller's tenant. Returns the newly-created Member.

request.description: Consumes a one-time accept token. The caller's JWT supplies the user identity; the invitation's stored tenant_id is constant-time-compared to the caller's tenant. Returns the newly-created Member.

item.name: /v1/organizations/:organization_id/invitations
item.description: Returns 202 Accepted because the email dispatch is queued via the Notifications module. The response carries `accept_url` and the one-time plaintext token alongside `state` + `expires_at`; subsequent reads of this invitation return only the `token_prefix`. Never log the response body.

request.description: Returns 202 Accepted because the email dispatch is queued via the Notifications module. Send and inspect transactional notifications. POST /send returns 202

item.description: Returns 202 Accepted; Novu trigger happens via the outbox worker so Novu downtime does not block the request response. Status transitions live on the worker — clients poll GET /v1/notifications/{id}.

item.name: users
item.description:
Identity façade for the data plane. Wraps Keycloak; consumers never
see Keycloak details. Email and other PII are envelope-encrypted at
rest (see AGENTS.md §18.7).

item.description: Idempotent. The platform creates a row + a Keycloak user in the shared `saas-data-local` realm (per-Deployment realm lands in Phase 12). Email is envelope-encrypted; an HMAC-SHA256 lookup hash backs the per-tenant uniqueness index.

item.description: Returns the platform users belonging to the caller's tenant. Email plaintext is returned (decrypted at the persistence boundary); the envelope columns stay on the server. Set the `email` query parameter to look up a single user by email (HMAC-prefix lookup; never sends plaintext to the DB).

audit
item.description:
Append-only audit log with a per-tenant SHA-256 hash chain
(AGENTS.md §8.6, §18.3, ADR 012). Rows enter the table only via
the outbox subscriber; the HTTP surface is read-only. Each row
carries prev_hash and row_hash so external auditors can verify
integrity via the control-plane /audit-integrity endpoint
without trusting the data-plane. Canonicalisation is RFC 8785
JCS — see ADR 012.
